summary: Build practical HACCP plans, hygiene programs, and audit-ready food safety systems in this 5-day intermediate course. Enroll your team today.
lede: Food safety management training helps professionals in food operations build and maintain controls for hazards across handling and production. Participants learn to map processes, assess biological, chemical and physical hazards, set critical control limits, and document hygiene and sanitation programs. They also practice monitoring records, internal audits and corrective actions within an ISO 22000-aligned food safety system.
audienceIntro: This food safety, HACCP and hygiene management training is built for professionals who already work in food operations and need to formalize, strengthen, or audit their control systems.
modules: Food Safety Risk Context and Foundations
Codex HACCP Principles and Process Mapping
Hazard Analysis, CCPs, and Critical Limits Design
Monitoring, Verification, Internal Audits, and Digital Tools
Incident Management, Non-conformities, and Corrective Actions
Supplier Control, Training, Culture, and Implementation Roadmap
prerequisites: This is an intermediate-level course. You should have: Basic familiarity with food handling operations in manufacturing, catering, retail, or distribution. Exposure to any food safety program, inspection, or audit process. Ability to read and complete technical forms, logs, and checklists in English. Access to examples of your organization’s current procedures or records (recommended, not mandatory). No coding or advanced IT skills are required. Technology concepts such as digital temperature logging, sensor data, and simple dashboards are taught at operational application level so you can specify, interpret, and use outputs, not engineer systems.
